target_concept: season total value on recorded opportunities
positions_supported: attack, midfield, faceoff, goalie, defensive_field (separately, never pooled)
baseline: league-average conversion on the SAME opportunity class
cross_position_claim: NONE -- explicitly single-role only
double_counting_risk: NONE (EPA_points_raw is the accounting-safe sum; see dependency file)
reliability: high within role (sums exactly to 0 league-wide)
validation_result: PASS accounting; PASS within-role rank stability is season-specific (see validation results)
major_assumptions: League-average opportunity baseline is the right counterfactual; a shot/faceoff/touch is the right unit of opportunity.
major_failure_modes: None once scoped to a single role -- this IS what Phase 6/8 already publish.

target_concept: season total value, ranked across all roles
positions_supported: ALL ROLES ON ONE LIST
cross_position_claim: YES -- this is exactly the composite the brief forbids
double_counting_risk: NONE at the accounting level, but ranks by opportunity volume
reliability: high per-component, but the RANKING inherits each role's own reliability profile
validation_result: FAIL cross-position: role SD ratio 4.58x pooled (2.0-8.6x by season); 13.7% of the top decile is below-median-opportunity
major_assumptions: That opportunity-count differences of up to 21x across roles do not need correcting.
major_failure_modes: Ranks players by how much of their job the feed happens to count, not by contribution (CROSS_POSITION_VALUE_RESEARCH.md sec 1, method M01).

target_concept: value per possession, attributed to the player who touched it
positions_supported: any
cross_position_claim: would require testing
double_counting_risk: would inherit MF1's issues plus a new attribution problem
sample_size_requirement: requires lineup/on-off data this feed does not have
validation_result: NOT RUN: no player-level possession-exposure denominator exists
major_assumptions: That a player can be tied to the possessions his team ran while he was on the field.
major_failure_modes: The feed carries NO lineup, substitution or on-field data of any season (PLAYER_VALUE_ACCOUNTING.md sec 6). A possession cannot be attributed to a player who did not touch the ball on it, and 'touched the ball' is exactly what shot/turnover/faceoff-denominated EPA already captures -- this model family collapses back into MF1 for the touches it CAN see and is UNSUPPORTED for the possession-level exposure it would need to add anything.

target_concept: caused-turnover value above position-group per-game rate
positions_supported: defensive_field
cross_position_claim: single-role only, and must never be compared to another role's total
double_counting_risk: LOW by construction, HIGH in spirit (see games_played confound in dependency file)
sample_size_requirement: n/a -- reliability of the underlying rate is not separately estimated (no beta-binomial rate exists for a single box-score count)
validation_result: PASS accounting; the underlying signal (caused turnovers) correlates rho=0.49-0.80 with games_played, i.e. up to 64% availability
major_assumptions: That caused turnovers, on a games-played denominator, capture defensive contribution.
major_failure_modes: Zero of 52,633 raw events name a causing or closest defender. This is a box-score total with an availability confound, not an impact measure. The word 'partial' must travel with every use.

target_concept: season value, using career-shrunk rate instead of the season's own rate
positions_supported: any role with an estimable rate
inputs: career-shrunk rate x season opportunity count
cross_position_claim: no more than MF3
double_counting_risk: MODERATE (re-derives the same production a second way)
sample_size_requirement: requires the player to have a career reliability >0
reliability: inherits career reliability (up to 85.1% for two-point selection, as low as 0% for two-point conversion)
validation_result: REJECTED on stated methodological grounds, not tested numerically: SHRINKAGE_POLICY.md sec 1 -- multiplying a shrunk RATE by the player's own opportunity COUNT drags every total toward zero in proportion to sample size, which is a materially stronger and unjustified claim ('this player produced less than he did') rather than the correct one ('we know less about him than we would like').
major_assumptions: That shrinking a rate and multiplying by the player's own volume is equivalent to shrinking a total.
major_failure_modes: It is not -- it conflates two different corrections.

target_concept: who IS the best (ability), not who HAD the best season (value)
positions_supported: shooting, one-point, faceoff, save, turnover-per-touch (career-estimable rates)
additive: n/a (not additive -- it is a rate)
cross_position_claim: single-role only, and answers a DIFFERENT question than a season award
double_counting_risk: NONE (this is not a value model, it is an ability estimate)
sample_size_requirement: reliability >=0.5 required to rank; 13.8%-54.4% of players clear it depending on rate
reliability: split-half reliability 0.47-0.58 (three well-populated rates, Spearman-Brown 0.64-0.74); save_pct only 0.10
major_assumptions: That a career average measures 'how good is this player right now'.
major_failure_modes: Ageing, role change and team context are modelled nowhere (44 players changed position, 97 changed team across 2022-2026).

target_concept: empirically derived cross-role weights, from team-level outcome regression
unit: coefficients relating role-summed EPA to team win_pct (unitless per-role weight, NOT comparable to a per-player weight)
positions_supported: attack+midfield (offense), faceoff, defensive_field, goalie -- at the TEAM level only
inputs: team-season sums of offensive_EPA_points_raw, faceoff_value_raw, defensive_value_partial_raw, goalie_value_raw
additive: yes, by construction of the linear model, but NOT validated as additive at the player level
cross_position_claim: This is the single most literal attempt in the project at Model Family 5, and it is included specifically to show why it fails as a WEIGHT SOURCE for an individual-level model despite a real, non-trivial in-sample fit.
double_counting_risk: MODERATE-HIGH: the response (win_pct) and predictors (EPA components) are computed from the SAME games, so part of the fit is definitional (a team that outscored expectation on offense in a game partly explains that game's win by definition)
sample_size_requirement: n=40 team-seasons for 4 predictors -- roughly 8-10 observations per coefficient, thin for any claim beyond sign and rough magnitude
reliability: not separately estimated (component reliabilities are role rates, not this regression's own coefficients)
validation_result: R^2 in-sample=0.663, leave-one-season-out R^2=0.526 (drops materially out of sample); bootstrap 95% CI on off_epa coefficient [0.0002, 0.0085] spans nearly 2x its own point estimate (0.0044)
major_assumptions: That team win_pct is a valid external criterion for deriving cross-role weights, and that a team-level coefficient can be redistributed to individual players.
major_failure_modes: (1) Circularity: EPA components are residuals against the same scoring outcomes that determine win_pct, so this substantially re-derives the definition of winning rather than validating it externally. (2) n=40 team-seasons for 4 predictors is too thin to trust coefficient magnitudes, even though none of their bootstrap CIs cross zero. (3) A team-level coefficient is not a per-player weight: off_epa aggregates ~15-20 field players per team-season while fo_epa/g_epa aggregate 1-3 specialists, so 'coefficient per point of off_epa' and 'coefficient per point of fo_epa' are not naturally comparable at the player level without an additional, unvalidated assumption about within-role distribution. (4) It says nothing about which individual teammate produced a team's EPA.

target_concept: measured defensive PRODUCTION (not value, not ability, not rank of impact)
unit: raw caused-turnover and ground-ball counts, disclosed WITH games played, never divided into a rate presented as ability
positions_supported: defensive_field
inputs: caused_turnovers, ground_balls, games_played (all three shown, never combined into one score)
baseline: none -- this is a production count, not a value model
cross_position_claim: NONE, and no value claim of any kind
double_counting_risk: NONE (it is intentionally not a value model)
reliability: not applicable (a count, not an estimate)
validation_result: honest by construction: it claims only what it is
major_assumptions: That showing three raw counts side by side, without a combined score, is not itself a ranking claim requiring the same rigor as a value model.
major_failure_modes: A reader may still misread a sorted table as a ranking; the strongest defensible practice is to leave the leaderboard UNSORTED by any single column, or sort by games played (an availability fact) rather than by production.
